To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) aminoglycose-resistant Streptococus and Enterococcus were found in bovine mammary infections; 2) resistance was not due to plasmids or mobilizable plasmids; and 3) the mechanisms of resistance are unknown.

aminoglycide-resistant streptococci and enterococci isolated from bovine milk were found to be resistant to streptomycin more than to kanamycin and gentamicin, and the resistance was not due to plasmids or plasmid-mediated conjugative transfer.
aminoglycocide resistance is prevalent in bovine mammary streptococci and enterococci and that the resistance is not mediated by plasmid transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation of antibiotic resistant bacteria from the bovine udder, the identification of these organisms, the mechanism(s) of resistance to aminoglycose antibiotics and the epidemiology of these organisms in dairy herds.
the identification of the mechanisms of aminoglicoside resistance in Streptococcus spp. and Enterococcus spp. from bovine mammmaries.

the aminoglycocide resistance in the bovine mammary isolates is due to a combination of mechanisms, including the presence of plasmids and/or conjugative transposon, as well as chromosomal mutations.
aminoglycocides are not a useful treatment for bovine mastitis.
the aminoglycocides are not effective for the treatment of mastitis caused by Streptococcus spp. and E. faecium, but they are effective for mastitis caused by E. faecales.

we have shown that aminoglycoiside resistant streptococci and enterococci are prevalent in bovine mammary infections.
